 MACC and China's NCS look to strengthen cooperation against corruption
 By FARIK ZOLKEPLI 
 Friday, 20 Nov 2026
 | 9:52 AM MYT

 MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman (left) receives a souvenir from China’s National Commission of Supervision vice-chairman and Central Commission for Discipline Inspection deputy secretary-general Sun Xinyang during the latter’s courtesy visit to the MACC headquarters in Putrajaya on Thursday (Nov 19). 
 KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) and China's National Commission of Supervision (NCS) are looking to strengthen bilateral cooperation in corruption prevention, investigations and enforcement.
 The matter was discussed during a courtesy visit by an NCS delegation to the MACC headquarters on Thursday (Nov 19).
 The delegation was led by NCS vice-chairman and Central Commission for Discipline Inspection (CCDI) deputy secretary-general Sun Xinyang.
 The visit aimed to strengthen ties between the two institutions through the exchange of views, sharing of experiences and exploring opportunities for closer cooperation in combating corruption.
 MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said cooperation between the two agencies had continued to grow since the signing of a memorandum of understanding (MoU) on Oct 17, 2023.
 He said the MoU, which is valid for five years with automatic renewal, served as an important foundation for strengthening joint efforts to combat corruption.
 "Hopefully, this meeting will open up more opportunities for cooperation between both institutions, particularly through the sharing of expertise and experience to enhance the effectiveness of corruption prevention and enforcement efforts," he said.
